blinding_statement: Reviewed only the supplied blind packet. No hidden-cell guess or provenance inference was made.

methodology.unit: One complete sixteen-turn conversation across both scenes
procedure: Read both scenes and the between-scene history before assigning any rating.
Treat a stylish isolated line as insufficient unless objectives, replies, status, and consequences remain legible across the whole exchange.
Rate unsupported scene facts, continuity errors, prompt-metadata echoes, generic therapy language, clipped repetition, and aphoristic symmetry as quality costs rather than as character depth.
Use turn indices as concise evidence; a pass requires affirmative dramatic evidence, mixed indicates partial or uneven evidence, and fail indicates absence or contradiction.

observations: The strongest conversations make an earlier promise, refusal, question, or interpretive concession constrain scene two.
The weakest conversations abandon scene-one pressure for menu ordering, setup, or mechanically narrated rehearsal, preserving coherence without dramatic consequence.

Okabe and Kurisu are usually easy to distinguish, but repeated experiment-versus-correction banter often becomes a catchphrase machine; the better cases let the performance crack or make Mayuri's routine costly.

Setsuna, Haruki, and Kazusa are strongest when precise questions expose permission, avoidance, or relationship debt; they weaken when everyone speaks in polished boundary-setting language or merely repeats known facts.

Prominent grounding faults include leaked speaker labels, exact scene-metadata recitation, gender inconsistency, an absent bun or cup reappearing, route contradiction, and a causal claim stronger than the speakers' knowledge.
